sources.entry: Muxy - AI-native GUI for managing AI coding sessions, projects, with split panes, Git integration, and AI usage tracking.

summary.one_liner: Muxy is a lightweight, memory-efficient terminal multiplexer built with Rust, GPUI and libghostty, with desktop, CLI, and mobile companion options.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Muxy as a terminal multiplexer built with Rust, GPUI and libghostty. Its listed top-level features include background sessions, remote sessions, split panes, Git worktrees, extensions, AI coding agent integrations, 490+ themes, and a TUI. It also mentions mobile companion apps for iOS and Android. A standalone muxy CLI and server can run on macOS and Linux without the desktop app. Full documentation is hosted externally at docs, and the README itself does not detail the feature set further. The AI usage tracking and GUI session management mentioned in the awesome-mac listing are not described in this README.
use_cases: run and manage terminal sessions in the background
split a terminal window into multiple panes
work with Git worktrees from a terminal tool
use a terminal multiplexer on macOS or Linux
control terminal sessions from a mobile device
how_to_run: Or download the DMG for your Mac from the latest release
On Ubuntu 24.04: use the quick installer, or download a .deb or AppImage from the latest release
notable: Built on Rust, GPUI and libghostty for low memory use
Separate muxy CLI and server that run without the desktop app
Mobile companion apps for iOS and Android
caveats: Linux support is described as experimental, targeting x86_64 and ARM64
The desktop app requires macOS 14 or newer
Linux install instructions are specifically for Ubuntu 24.04 in the README
